scope: Visual design and workflow quality; source-only follow-up with no Android runtime validation
critique: I treated the next planned workout as the natural filled action. ADR-021 explicitly reserves that action for freestyle and planned rows open confirmation. Preserve this and test clearer differentiation and stat ordering (UX01).
Pinned commit area, large controls, undo and keyboard/landscape work already exist. Improve transitions, feedback and data-entry truth rather than rebuilding them (UX03/UX06).
The literal Next label exists. Add destination context without forcing a long exercise name into a single fixed line (UX03/UX24).
A RestDock already sits outside scrolling content. Validate the next-set/rest/keyboard interaction and failure states; do not create a duplicate timer surface (UX03).
Current Other choices disclosure is intentional. Preview bulk consequences after the user chooses Move/Adapt/Skip, rather than expanding all choices on Home (UX14).
History already has totals, calendar, sessions, blocks and records. The main questions are scope and reachability. Do not add a sixth tab or automatically add multiple nested tab bars (UX15/UX16).

A substantial receipt with working sets, duration, records, breakdown, Done and full-session actions already exists. The newly verified problem is truthfulness of missing/failure states, plus choice of meaningful headline metric (UX05).
Shared anatomy is useful, but different activity types legitimately support different fields/actions. Use an explicit capability matrix and draft/save contract, not identical screens (UX07/UX29).
Display-first and prominent Export are accepted decisions. Pushing them into a generic directory may add friction. Compare modest disclosure before replacing the page (UX20).

The code already has 48/56/72 dp tokens. Real hit widths, keyboard interactions and full-screen accessibility still need testing; the seven-column strip shows why token presence is not proof (UX12/UX25).

items.title: Clarify Home's planned versus freestyle actions
items.type: Source-backed usability hypothesis
items.observation: Home is a selected-day board. ADR-021 reserves general Start a workout for the existing chooser (free, routine, cardio or Extra); planned rows open their named confirmation. Recent statistics are already removed from the Home board. The remaining visual packet clarifies the illustrated agenda and keeps generic Start reachable as it scrolls.
items.outcome: Users distinguish starting the listed planned session from choosing another activity and can identify the selected date.
requirements: Preserve planned-row confirmation, the current Home Start a workout sheet without an Add row (ADR-021), and the single ambient Live Session Bar.

Keep Start a workout opening the existing chooser. Do not describe all its choices as an empty session or silently change the accepted wording. Planned Start retains its own session identity and confirmation.
Keep the agenda before secondary check-ins and the week strip intact. Compare loaded, empty, missed-work and active-session states; the generic Start stays reachable while the agenda scrolls.
Show the full selected date in the masthead. When another day is selected, provide a quiet, accessible return-to-today action; make clear a live/free workout starts now rather than backdating.
Maintain only one dominant filled action in each state, including first visit and missed-work handling. Do not add another resume hero above the existing live bar.
acceptance: Given both a planned workout and freestyle control, a participant can correctly explain which follows the routine and which starts empty.
Given another selected day, starting/logging behavior matches explicit copy and existing date rules; no silent backdating.
At 360 dp and large text, the planned row's start action is discoverable without an unrelated statistics detour; measure rather than assert this has improved.
items.decision: Preserve ADR-021. Alternative primary-action semantics are a separate product decision.

items.title: Separate starting now from recording completed activity
items.type: Source-backed workflow refinement
items.observation: StartOptionsSheet already groups Log and Live cardio and is not hosted on Home. It also includes today's plan, suggested lift, every routine, free workout and manual logging; long routine lists can push recording actions far down.
items.outcome: Users can reach the right capture mode without interpreting a long menu of similar actions.
requirements: Retain the modal sheet and current Body/History/Plan entry points; do not add a full-screen start interstitial or sixth tab.
Use two clear headings: Start now and Record a completed activity. Keep today's planned option contextual and distinguish it from freestyle.
Bound the initial routine section with a browse/search disclosure when necessary; do not unconditionally show dozens of routines ahead of manual logging.
Label cardio choices by behavior: live timer versus enter completed time/distance. Preserve the selected return route and date when a caller supplies context.
When a session is active, retain the existing go-to-session explanation instead of offering an invalid second start.
acceptance: With 0, 3 and 50 routines, participants can find past strength, manual cardio, mixed entry and live cardio.
Selecting a manual entry does not start a timer; dismissing the sheet makes no training-data write.
Opening the sheet while a session runs produces one clear answer and no duplicate session.

The current native Home layout preserves those routes; broader StartOptions usability and participant tasks remain open.

items.title: Refine the existing logging dock and action transitions
items.type: Existing capability to preserve and refine
items.observation: The workout already has a 72 dp primary action, pinned dock, rest dock, undo offers, edit state and next-exercise transition. 'Next' is the clearest specific copy weakness; a brand-new logging dock would duplicate existing work.
items.outcome: A lifter knows exactly what the next tap commits and can correct a set quickly.
requirements: Keep the current dock's structural ownership, keyboard handling, load-type rules and landscape adaptations.
Replace ambiguous Next with a concise action tied to the next exercise, using a two-line adaptive label or adjacent context if the name is long. Preserve full accessible wording.
Distinguish typed draft, suggested target, currently editing saved set, saved receipt and saving state. Do not style a prefilled target as completed data.
After accepted log, show the exact saved result using SetCopy/load semantics, offer existing Undo, and put focus where the next meaningful entry begins without jumping unexpectedly.
Rest countdown remains visible while editing next-set inputs; an edit of a prior set should not inadvertently start or reset rest unless that is the defined behavior.
Make add-another-set and next-exercise both discoverable when planned sets finish. Keep Finish available but visually separate from the repetitive log action.
acceptance: Rapid repeated activation while a write is pending commits one set.
Warmup, bodyweight, added-weight and assisted movements show the correct labels and units; no universal '0 kg' assumption.
Keyboard open at 360 dp and landscape leaves the active field and commit action reachable.
Undo/edit/next transitions preserve exercise identity and announce accepted results once.

items.title: Make routine Save truthful and clarify autosave
items.type: Source-supported correctness defect plus interaction ambiguity
items.observation: RoutineEditorViewModel.persistDetailsOnExit catches update failure and continues leaving. saveAndLeave requests exit afterward; staged-target failures also do not form an aggregate success gate. The editor writes some changes immediately while Save and Back flush others. A user can press Save, leave, and later discover the rename/notes/targets did not persist.
items.outcome: Save either succeeds with durable changes or explains exactly what remains unsaved, with a retry and an explicit exit choice.
requirements: Return typed outcomes from all required flushes, including staged targets and details. Do not set exitRequested merely because the coroutine reached its end.
Retain failed draft content and clear leaving/busy state so Retry works. Propagate cancellation correctly.

Preserve ADR-021's Save affordance and existing write-through model. Explain it briefly: proposed 'Exercise changes save as you make them. Save finishes your name, notes and targets.' Prefer simplifying the persistence contract if feasible, but do not falsely imply Cancel can undo committed edits.
On Save failure stay with the draft and an actionable error. On Back with a write failure, offer Retry and Leave without saving the remaining edits; describe that already-saved changes remain.
Make saving state visible and prevent duplicate exit requests. Consider a common completion result for required writes rather than brittle message-string matching.
acceptance: Inject details-write failure after editing a name: Save remains on screen, preserves text and offers retry.
Inject one staged-target failure: no blanket success/exit; retry persists the intended value once.
Back after successful edits remains consistent with existing autosave; empty new stubs retain their documented cleanup.
Process recreation during failure retains sufficient draft state; reopening shows the accepted persisted result.

items.title: Separate saved receipts from missing or unavailable summaries
items.type: Source-supported correctness/copy defect
items.observation: WorkoutSummaryViewModel maps both a missing session and a summary-building exception to missing=true. WorkoutSummaryScreen renders 'Workout saved' and 'It is in your history' for missing or no-work cases. A genuinely missing row cannot support that assertion. The app already has a substantial completion receipt and pinned Done/View actions.
items.outcome: A user receives a trustworthy confirmation and useful next step even if analytics fail.
requirements: Represent accepted save receipt, successfully loaded session, no summarizable work, missing session and failed summary calculation separately.
If an accepted session ID/receipt is known but analytics fail, say 'Workout saved. Summary unavailable.' Offer retry/view history without resubmitting the workout.
If the row is genuinely absent and no current receipt establishes its presence, say it cannot be found; do not claim it is in History.
Retain current Done and full-session navigation, record semantics and reduced-motion behavior.

Audit the headline for bodyweight-only and mixed work: total kilograms must not be the sole hero when that quantity cannot represent the session. Choose a documented suitable summary without equating tonnage to quality.
acceptance: Missing ID, deleted/restored-over row, computation failure after confirmed save and valid no-work data each render distinct truthful states.
Retrying summary never creates or re-finishes a workout.
A bodyweight-only workout does not appear worthless because its load-volume is zero.
Back and Done exit once and do not return to an already-finished live session.

items.title: Stop numeric input from silently changing meaning
items.type: Source-supported input defect; host demonstrations only
items.observation: NumericEntry.filterDecimal strips signs and extra separators; integer fields use filter(Char::isDigit). Source-equivalent examples turn -50 into 50, 1.2.3 into 1.23 and 8.5 reps into 85. The parser correctly supports comma decimals and rejects some ambiguity, but filtering can transform the text before parsing sees it.
items.outcome: The number saved is the number the user knowingly entered, or the app clearly rejects it.
requirements: Preserve raw editable text until validation, or reject the whole invalid proposed edit without constructing a different numeric value. Do not salvage digits from arbitrary pasted text.
Retain support for a single decimal point or comma and meaningful intermediate edit states, such as blank or a trailing decimal separator.
Use field-specific validation: reps integer, duration constraints, optional distance, and correct load semantics. Keep errors next to the exact field.
Show the unit persistently; a unit switch must not reinterpret unchanged digits as a different physical quantity.
On commit, focus/scroll to the first invalid field and announce its error. Do not dismiss the form or silently reuse an old value.
Test paste, select-all replacement, hardware keyboard, IME composition and accessible entry. Define non-ASCII digits and grouping policy deliberately rather than guessing.
acceptance: 8.5 reps is rejected rather than saved as 85; -50 kg is rejected rather than saved as 50.
1.2.3 and 8e2 do not become different accepted values; 62,5 and 62.5 behave equivalently under the supported decimal policy.
Existing valid values survive unit conversion/round trips without drift beyond specified display precision.
All shared filter callers are covered, including composer, live cardio and routine targets.
The custom week's target boxes refuse what the week cannot hold; Confirm names the rule and stays, and fixing one card does not release another still unreadable.
items.status: Implemented locally; domain tests executed (JVM lane); routine-editor and custom-week card wiring included. The custom week was reached last, through the compile break the widened SessionLiftStrip signature caused: its boxes now refuse what the week cannot hold instead of applying the stored number underneath the shown one.

items.title: Define draft preservation and leave-during-save behavior
items.type: Known lifecycle gap plus workflow specification
items.observation: Composer ViewModel holds authored activity lists/title/date in memory, even though several individual input controls use rememberSaveable. Onboarding answers are also memory state. These are different layers: preserved text fields do not mean the complete draft survives. Composer Cancel remains interactive while saving.
items.outcome: Switching apps does not destroy assembled work, and leaving during a save cannot produce an ambiguous outcome.
requirements: Define a draft record per activity/editor flow with stable row/exercise IDs, date, units context and pending input where appropriate.
Use bounded saved state for compact UI values and private durable storage for larger or longer-lived drafts; do not store full history graphs in a Bundle.
Define explicit clear points: accepted save or deliberate discard, not transient navigation or a failed write.

Specify save-in-progress exit behavior. Preferred baseline: prevent destructive discard while commit status is unresolved, allow an explained background continuation only if a durable completion receipt is implemented.
On restored draft, disclose its date and provide Resume or Discard when context may be stale. Reconcile removed exercises without silently replacing them.
Clarify different guarantees for rotation, system process recreation, task removal, force-stop and device restart; promise only what the chosen persistence supports.
acceptance: Build a multi-row mixed draft, background, recreate the process and restore: date, rows, order and values survive.
Cancel/Back during delayed accepted save neither creates a duplicate nor tells the user committed work was discarded.
Failed save preserves the draft; successful save clears only that draft.
Onboarding draft restoration does not overwrite the saved current plan or create a new one without acceptance.

items.type: Source-backed layout risk; device reproduction required

Bodyweight also includes a 144 dp wheel. Large text/short windows can consume the space needed for Continue. The existing wheel already supports typed entry and optional skipping.
items.outcome: Setup remains usable at large text, short height and with assistive technology.
requirements: Use one consistent page shell with measured header, scrollable step content and a reachable action area where the step has Continue.
Preserve single-choice auto-advance unless comparison testing shows a problem; ensure Back returns to the answer and moving forward preserves it.
Keep bodyweight optional and keep its existing typed alternative; make that alternative visibly discoverable without requiring someone to guess the numeral is tappable.
Maintain question count for the actual selected focus path. Do not show a fixed count when cardio skips questions.
Restore draft step and answers through UX07; returning to setup must distinguish a draft from stored preferences.
Test existing-program preview and show that routines are added alongside existing ones; avoid a misleading replacement story.
acceptance: Every question and Continue/Skip action is reachable at 360×640 dp, font 2.0, and the smaller supported window configuration.
Typed bodyweight, wheel, unit switch and Skip produce consistent optional values.
Screen-reader focus lands on the new question and Back keeps the selected answer.
Accepting a plan once creates the intended program; reopening setup does not silently apply a draft.

items.title: Carry an exercise through Create routine
items.type: Source-backed workflow gap
items.observation: Library's AddToRoutineSheet tells users with no routines to create one first, then add the lift. Its onCreateRoutine callback dismisses the selected exercise and navigates without carrying it. The user must find the same exercise again.
items.outcome: Choosing an exercise and creating a first routine feels like one continuous task.
requirements: Carry the selected exercise ID as an explicit pending add intent into routine creation, rather than retaining a mutable Exercise object in an unrelated screen.
Show the selected lift in the new routine draft or clearly confirm it will be added on acceptance, with normal defaults visible.
Define cancellation: no orphan empty routine, no unexpected exercise addition to another routine, and a return to the original library context.
Preserve query, muscle/equipment filters and scroll position on return.
Handle exercise deletion or duplicate membership before completion with an actionable state; do not substitute another exercise.
acceptance: From an empty routine catalogue, choose a lift → Create routine → save: exactly one routine contains that lift, without another search.
Cancel returns to the original context and leaves no empty stub.
Rotation/process recreation retains the pending exercise ID according to the draft contract.

items.title: Reduce accidental custom-exercise creation and keep picker errors visible
items.type: Source-supported behavior mismatch and modal error risk
items.observation: The picker comment says creation appears when nothing matches, but canCreate tests only absence of an exact name; 'bench' can therefore show Create above valid partial results. Creation is a repository write even before an activity is saved. Picker error rendering is inside the MULTI_ADD branch, and single-select callers may report errors behind the sheet.
items.outcome: Search leads to existing lifts first; creating a new lift is explicit and errors appear where the action occurred.
requirements: Show good partial results before a secondary Create custom lift option, or require an explicit create intent. Do not equate 'not an exact match' with 'no matches'.
Use a clearly named create step with required muscle/load metadata supported by the current model; preserve duplicate-name checks.

Explain the persistence boundary: creating a catalogue lift may survive cancelling an activity. Alternatively implement a staged-create design, with explicit scope and tests, rather than promising rollback that does not exist.
Render busy and error state in all picker modes, including single select and create. Keep the query and chosen muscle when creation fails.
Keep the existing multi-select ordered cart. Define whether dismissal clears unconfirmed picks and prevent dismissal from concealing an accepted add-in-progress result.
acceptance: Searching 'bench' with existing matching variants prioritizes choosing them over creating 'bench'.
Duplicate/disk/create errors are visible within the active sheet in single and multi modes.
Create then cancel activity follows the disclosed catalogue persistence rule.
Double confirmation adds the selected IDs once and preserves order.

items.title: Make edit scope and secondary actions discoverable
items.type: Source-backed interaction refinement
items.observation: Routine edits write through; routine deletion is long-press with an accessible action label; swaps are constrained to movement siblings. These deliberate behaviors must not be replaced by a generic editor. Users still need to know whether they are changing today's workout, a reusable routine, or a recurring schedule.
items.outcome: Editing one thing does not unexpectedly alter future training, and users can find management actions without guessing gestures.
requirements: Label edit scope in the appropriate sheet/header: This workout, Routine, or Every Tuesday, using actual affected entities.

Preserve long-press as a shortcut but consider a quiet accessible overflow as an additional discoverable route to routine management. Keep the existing delete confirmation and history-preservation explanation.
Retain same-movement swap choices and target preservation. Explain whether the choice affects just this session or the stored routine before acceptance.
Do not introduce machine-specific photo portfolios, new load histories or schema changes as part of this polish packet.
Offer undo only when the operation is truly reversible; distinguish remove-from-routine from delete-catalogue-item.
acceptance: A participant can state the scope before saving a swap or schedule edit.
Routine management is reachable without relying solely on long press, or documented usability evidence supports retaining the existing affordance.
Deleting a routine preserves history and accurately explains its impact on scheduled days.
items.decision: Adding a discoverable alternative is a proposal; preserve existing shortcuts and scope.

items.title: Make calendar dates and statuses distinguishable at small widths
items.type: Layout arithmetic risk plus semantic refinement
items.observation: WeekStrip divides seven cells equally after 16 dp side gutters and six 4 dp gaps. At 360 dp this is about 43.4 dp per cell, below a 48 dp target width. HeightIn only sets height. Compose touch expansion may alter hit bounds, so actual overlap needs inspection. Day fill also means resolved planned blocks, where skipped and done can both contribute to ALL.
items.outcome: Users tap the intended date and understand today, selection, planned work, completed work and skipped work.
requirements: Measure actual hit bounds and adjacent overlap on supported widths; do not claim height alone establishes target compliance.

Explore a local edge-to-edge strip variant at narrow widths while preserving overall page gutters elsewhere. At widths where seven 48 dp targets cannot fit, provide an accessible alternative date selection path and document any exception to the current non-scrolling strip rule.
Keep a full selected-date heading and full spoken date, including month/year where ambiguity exists. Single-letter weekday labels must not be the only identification.
Distinguish resolved schedule from completed exercise. Retain the model but use a labelled detail such as '1 completed · 1 skipped'; do not call both workouts completed.
Use text/icon/state semantics alongside color, particularly for future planned days and selected/today differences.
Check History's month padding days and spoken labels, which currently begin with day-of-month alone.
acceptance: At 320/360/412 dp, date targets are measurable and usable without overlapping ambiguous activation regions, or an equivalent accessible selector is supplied.
A week containing done, skipped, missed, future and rest days has unambiguous spoken and visible detail.
Selecting a neighboring-month date opens the correct civil date; today remains distinguishable from selection.
items.decision: Changing the seven-day non-scrolling presentation needs an explicit accessibility/layout decision; do not shrink targets to preserve it.
items.status: Proposed; no implementation or Android runtime validation performed

items.title: Expose recurrence and ordering consequences without restoring clock clutter

items.outcome: Users know whether an addition repeats and whether rearranging it changes reminder/order behavior.
requirements: Keep the existing Home keep-choice and Plan weekly behavior. State the scope near the final action: 'This Tuesday only' versus 'Every Tuesday'.

Audit Up/Down side effects against the repository implementation. Disclose relevant reminder/future-order effects; do not describe it as cosmetic if persisted hours/rules change.
Do not restore clock pickers or drag-only ordering in this packet. If reminder order must be independent of visible order, document it as a separate model/product decision with schema impact.
For past-day or blocked edits, show why the action is unavailable instead of a silent no-op.
acceptance: Add the same type once and recurring in separate scenarios; next week contains only the recurring case.
Reordering states exactly which future/reminder behavior changes and preserves completed history.
Home and Plan show the same dated occurrences after changes.

items.title: Make History's scope and deeper sections reachable

Declare scope for each section. If the horizon controls only totals, label that explicitly; if it filters sessions, implement and test the actual filtering.

Editing a prior best refreshes visible results and record drill-down identifies the supporting session.

items.title: Make chart axes, comparisons and sparse data honest
items.type: Source-backed visualization contract gap
items.observation: TrendChart already separates zero-based additive bars from range-scaled lines and supplies headline values/deltas. LineTrend spaces points uniformly by index, while ExerciseDetail labels the endpoints with session dates. That is valid for a session-index chart, but can imply uniform elapsed time if presented as a time axis.
items.outcome: Users can interpret the size, period and basis of a change without assuming the chart proves more than it does.
requirements: Choose and state the x-axis contract: equally spaced sessions labelled as sessions, or actual timestamps positioned proportionally. Do not change visual spacing without agreeing the meaning.
Provide chart title, unit, date/session range, current value and comparison basis. Include accessible exact values or a compact data list for detailed inspection.
Handle 0, 1, 2, flat, irregularly spaced and outlier points deliberately; do not draw a fabricated trend in an empty state.
Label estimated 1RM as estimated and preserve load-type eligibility; do not imply tonnage is universal strength progress.
Use a visible scale cue or range explanation for zoomed line charts, and keep bar zero baselines. A small improvement must not look enormous without context.
Compare like periods and comparable measures; specify current partial week/month versus equal elapsed prior period or clearly label full-period comparison.
acceptance: Jan 1, Jan 2 and Apr 1 samples do not imply equal elapsed intervals without an explicit session-axis label.
Screen-reader/data-list users can recover values and dates without relying on the plotted line.
Bodyweight-rep series use reps, loaded series use the selected physical unit, and empty/flat series are truthful.

items.title: Explain the body map as recorded muscle workload

All muscles remain reachable via full-size text rows with equivalent detail/actions.

items.title: Support mixed unit preferences deliberately
items.type: Product opportunity; not a regression defect
items.observation: DistanceUnit.fromWeight links kg to km and lbs to miles. People may prefer pounds for lifting and kilometers for running. My earlier generic Units recommendation did not identify this actual behavior or its data contract.
items.outcome: Users choose weight and distance displays independently without altering stored measurements.
requirements: Prototype separate Weight and Distance controls with current coupled behavior as the compatibility default for existing users.
Keep stored canonical units unchanged and convert only at display/input boundaries.
If implemented, include the new preference in backup, restore, migration/defaulting and onboarding/settings propagation. Do not add a UI-only toggle that some screens ignore.
Define what happens when a unit changes with an uncommitted draft: preserve the physical quantity where known or retain the original labelled input until explicitly converted.

Changing preference does not change stored distance or weight.

items.title: Reduce Settings scanning without burying recovery
items.type: Information architecture hypothesis constrained by ADRs
items.observation: Settings is intentionally the fifth tab, Display is first, and Export is its main filled action. A generic directory redesign that pushes backup several levels deep would undermine a documented recovery task. My earlier proposal was too unconditional.
items.outcome: Frequently needed preferences are scannable and recovery remains easy to find.
requirements: Compare the current page against a modest section-jump/progressive-disclosure variant before a full directory redesign.
Retain Display at the top and the prominent export entry per current decisions, unless evidence supports a documented change.
Use compact summaries for expandable coaching/equipment/reminder sections, so the user can inspect current settings before entering them.
Keep debug-only diagnostics/foundation controls confined to debug behavior; do not mistake their presence in a development build for production clutter.
Every new subpage needs a descriptive title, correct Back behavior and preservation of current tab state.
Do not add an empty Appearance section or manual reduce-motion toggle just because a generic settings template has one; expose only supported behavior.
acceptance: A participant can change units/rest preferences and find export/restore with no worse success than the baseline.
Reopening Settings restores useful context without hiding an unresolved save error.
Production and debug build screenshots are evaluated separately.
items.decision: Prototype first; do not automatically replace Settings with a directory.

items.title: Specify backup/recovery as a truthful multi-stage task
items.type: Known engineering dependencies plus interaction refinement
items.observation: Settings already has protected export, explicit plaintext warning, backup/restore timestamps, safety copies, import preview and consent flow. The main need is coherent progress, partial outcome and recovery messaging—not inventing a backup feature.
items.outcome: Users understand what is being exported/restored, what stage has completed and what they can safely do next.
requirements: Preserve a local-file route without Google sign-in. Explain Drive as optional backup access rather than an app account.
Show factual status: last successful export/upload, destination and protection when known. Do not infer recoverability from a timestamp or display 'Everything is safe'.
Use identifiable phases: reading, unlocking, checking, ready to review, restoring and finishing. Use determinate progress only where a real denominator exists.
Before replacement show backup date/source, data counts, unfinished-session exclusions/refusal and the actual replacement scope. Keep destructive acceptance explicit.

After partial failure, display what committed, what remains and the available retry. Do not advertise cancellation once an irreversible commit boundary has passed; explain safe leave/background behavior.
Make the difference between portable protected backups and plaintext local safety copies clear. Do not promise password reset for a password-derived file.
Integrate paged older Drive backups and expired/denied authorization states without losing the user's selection.
acceptance: Wrong password, oversized input, unsupported version, offline Drive, live workout, partial preferences failure and completed restore each have a distinct actionable screen.
Displayed success follows the actual accepted operation; no UI-only fix masks R01–R04.
Back/rotation/permission return retains the operation's correct stage and never repeats a destructive commit.
items.status: Proposed; no implementation or Android runtime validation performed

items.title: Preserve context through navigation, notifications and external screens
items.type: Cross-route validation gap; existing navigation mechanisms
items.observation: AppNav already saves/restores tab state, uses one live bar, and hands reminder taps through Home. These are strengths. The remaining task is end-to-end behavior when a picker, system permission, Google consent or notification interrupts another screen.
items.outcome: Users return to the task they were doing without duplicate screens, stale actions or lost filters.
requirements: Inventory every entry/exit path: normal tap, system Back, close icon, notification body/action, activity recreation and external permission/consent result.
Define precedence when a notification arrives over a dirty draft: preserve the draft and avoid a silent destructive navigation.
Consume deep-link navigation exactly once and re-read the target state. Missing/finished/moved sessions need a meaningful destination rather than a crash or phantom live view.
Retain tabs, pushed-route hierarchy and the single live bar. Do not add another resume card to solve discoverability locally.
On return from exercise detail, routine creation or permission Settings, restore query/filter/scroll and refresh the permission status without resetting the whole page.
acceptance: Repeated delivery/recreation of the same reminder intent does not stack duplicate live screens or start twice.
Returning from system settings keeps the active session/draft and reflects the real permission result.
Back from a completed summary cannot reopen the finished workout as live.
items.status: Proposed; no implementation or Android runtime validation performed

items.title: Create a shared language for loading, failure, saving and retry
items.type: Cross-cutting correctness contract
items.observation: Existing health wrappers and banners distinguish some strength paths well, but activity reads and summary/routine outcomes do not consistently use the same meanings. Composer errors can appear at the top of a long list while the user is at the bottom pressing Save.
items.outcome: Every message tells users what happened, whether their work exists and what action helps.
requirements: Define stable UI outcomes: loading, empty, available, stale-but-readable, unavailable, invalid input, saving, saved, partially saved and operation failed.
Tie each message to evidence from the operation; never map an exception directly to missing or claim saved solely because navigation reached a summary route.
Keep field errors inline; show form-save errors near the action and move focus to the relevant field. Avoid relying on a scrolled-away banner.
Retry must be idempotent and preserve input. A successful retry clears the correct error; unrelated success does not conceal unresolved failure.
Use short factual titles, one useful explanation and an action. Replace opaque wording such as 'pull may be behind' with 'Recent changes may not be shown' when that is the actual state.
Use a persistent/recoverable surface for critical failure; transient banners remain for non-critical confirmations.
acceptance: Injected initial/later load failures, invalid fields and post-commit side-effect failures produce the defined states.
Users can locate the error and retry at the point of action without losing authored data.
Missing, empty and unavailable never share a misleading generic success or start-new-workout remedy.

items.title: Apply responsive type and layout rules to actual content
items.type: Validation gap and source-backed truncation risks
items.observation: The token system already uses a 4 dp spacing grid, tabular numerals, 48/56/72 dp controls and adaptive helpers. Several names and explanatory captions still use one-line ellipsis; three-column metric rows can be crowded at large fonts. Another design-system rewrite would be wasteful.
items.outcome: Important names, values and instructions remain readable without making every screen visually noisy.
requirements: Keep current token values as the baseline. Modify shared components only after real layout evidence identifies a problem.
Define content priority: action label, identifying name, value+unit, error, explanation, decorative detail. Preserve the first five before shrinking or hiding them.
Allow meaningful names to wrap or provide an explicit full-name detail; variants with identical truncated prefixes must remain distinguishable at selection.
Stack metric rows at constrained width/font, not only based on a device class. Keep each number and unit together.
Do not shrink large user fonts to force a design to fit. Use scrolling, wrapping and layout changes.
Test large numbers, long exercise/routine names, empty names under validation, landscape, split window and system insets. Keep debug chrome out of production comparisons.

items.title: Tune feedback timing without adding decorative motion
items.type: Existing behavior to preserve and validate
items.observation: Reduced motion already follows system settings; records carry non-color cues. LiveSessionBar auto-clears action errors after a fixed six seconds. Important messages may need accessibility-adjusted dwell or a persistent recovery path. More animation is not automatically more polish.
items.outcome: Feedback is noticeable, readable and calm, including when animations are disabled.
requirements: Keep token-based motion and current palette; no new accent colors or bespoke milliseconds scattered across screens.

Ensure save confirmation follows accepted persistence, not just a tap. Haptics supplement visible feedback and respect system/user settings.
Keep critical failed-save/restore errors recoverable instead of disappearing with their only action.
Limit chart/record replay after rotation or unrelated state updates; reduced motion shows final information immediately without hiding it.
Measure transitions on a real device for focus/scroll jumps rather than adding effects to a static mockup.
acceptance: With reduced motion enabled, all data and records appear immediately and remain accessible.

items.title: Make exercise discovery precise and stateful
items.type: Existing capability to preserve and refine
items.observation: Library already has separate muscle and equipment filters, movement families, collision handling and shared exercise rows with the picker. Recommendations to 'add search/filtering' would be redundant. The next questions concern filter visibility, long-name disambiguation and return context.
items.outcome: Users find the intended equipment variant quickly and understand why results are empty.
requirements: Keep muscle AND equipment semantics and family grouping. Show active filters and a clear way to reset them without erasing the query unnecessarily.
Distinguish no results because of filters from no matching exercise and from failed catalogue load.
Preserve search/filter/expanded-family/scroll state across detail and routine-add round trips, including the new UX09 continuation.
Evaluate aliases/recently used choices with actual catalogue data before adding a new search engine; keep IDs and duplicate-name rules stable.
Make custom-versus-built-in collisions understandable without merging histories automatically.
For long variants, expose equipment and enough full name to distinguish the intended movement before committing.
acceptance: A participant finds a specified muscle+equipment variant and clears a restrictive filter without losing orientation.
Returning from detail restores the original results position.
Load failure does not invite creating a duplicate exercise because the catalogue appeared empty.

items.title: Improve setup preview and returning-user orientation
items.type: Source-backed refinement; existing setup is already optional
items.observation: Home already offers Generate, Build my own and Start workout without a mandatory onboarding gate. items.outcome: Users understand what will be created and can adjust it without restarting the entire setup.
requirements: Preserve all three first-visit paths and dismissibility; do not force bodyweight, Google sign-in or a plan before training.

Prevent double acceptance and keep a recoverable draft on generation/write failure.

acceptance: A user can inspect the proposed week, change equipment/days and return to an updated preview with other answers preserved.

items.title: Make activity-type differences explicit in details and receipts
items.type: Known capability divergence; product consistency specification
items.observation: Strength and typed activities have separate detail/summary paths. History offers Repeat only for legacy workout entries. Consistency should mean predictable contracts, not identical fields or invented feature parity.
items.outcome: Users know which actions are supported for each activity and see meaningful summaries for that activity type.
requirements: Create a capability matrix for live strength, backdated strength, live cardio, manual cardio, mixed and auxiliary sessions: edit, repeat, delete, records, plan linkage and receipt.
Retain legitimate type-specific measures; cardio should not inherit strength volume labels and bodyweight work should not become 0 kg.
Make unavailable actions clear where users would reasonably expect them. Do not expose a button that silently does nothing.
Define a consistent detail anatomy: identity/date/type, primary measures, contents, supported actions and data-health state.
Preserve the user's return context and avoid treating historical activity detail as a new completion celebration on every visit.
Implement new edit/repeat capabilities only after data-model and regression scope are explicit; matching visual buttons alone is insufficient.
acceptance: Each supported type has an accurate receipt and correct units with clear action capabilities.
Opening history detail does not replay a misleading new-save confirmation.
Repeat/edit where supported preserves correct IDs, chronology and plan linkage and cannot silently convert one type to another.

items.title: Establish an evidence-led design delivery and regression process
items.type: Quality/process work package
items.observation: No actual app screenshots or physical usability sessions were produced during this review. A high-fidelity speculative mockup cannot substitute for baseline production captures. Existing ADRs contain an evidence gate for changes to global navigation.
items.outcome: Design work produces a demonstrably easier app rather than a sequence of untested restyles.
requirements: Capture the current production screens and state variants on a pinned build before changing shared components.
Use this handoff's fixtures/tasks and record baseline completion, wrong turns, correction success and observed failure—not subjective polish alone.
Prototype only uncertain IA/visual decisions, especially Home ordering and Settings structure. Keep definite correctness fixes independent.
Implement in focused batches, compare the same fixtures before/after and maintain a decision log for any ADR amendment.
Record actual device/API/window/font/navigation/keyboard configuration with each capture. Keep golden profile stable; do not approve replacement images just because tests fail.
Publish a final evidence table of implemented, validated, deferred and blocked items. Preserve local privacy and do not add analytics to measure this personal app.
acceptance: Each implemented UX item has acceptance evidence, source/commit links and limitations.
Global-navigation changes follow the repository's current comparative task gate; no extra tab appears from taste alone.
Required device/accessibility gaps remain visibly open until actually tested.

testInfrastructure.problem: A full unit run on JDK 21 aborted when the C2 compiler crashed while compiling Room, so Gradle counted only the tests that had finished (4512 of about 4709) and exited 134. Separate from that, some tests saw a result while the operation was still marked busy, or read a screen value before the cached screen state had published the new day or the restored draft.
testInfrastructure.fix: Unit tests exclude C2 compilation of Room's prepare method so a JDK 21 compiler crash cannot abort the process and drop the unfinished tests. History repeat, history delete, and session-detail Resume publish their result only after the busy flag is clear. Notes stay locked during the repeat database call. Home Skip waits until the blocked start has finished. The week test waits for the new day. Undo's set clock is read after that clock flow publishes the restored seconds. Clearing notes holds the write across focus release. Artwork sampling waits until two frames agree, then keeps the 91 percent identity check. Session detail keeps an open Add when a read fails and opens a fresh sheet when the session comes back, instead of treating the missing snapshot as the lift being gone.

productFixes.problem: Swapping a lift and typing a weight, then reps and effort, could save the reps and the effort and store the weight as 0. The fill for the new lift decides the entry is untouched on a background read, and that decision used to be applied after the weight was typed. The checkpoint then kept the typed reps and effort and lost the typed weight.
productFixes.fix: The decision and the write now happen together, and the decision is checked again at the moment of the write. A weight typed in that gap is kept. Reps and effort already shared that save; they were not on a separate path.

productFixes.problem: Reviews after the typed-weight save and the weigh-in delete found that a routine upload could move a cloud delete's clock and the next download could erase a newer local weigh-in. A restore could also queue the days from before the restore, and an older delete waiting to upload could erase a newer weigh-in already in the cloud.
productFixes.fix: An upload sends the day stored on the phone and reads the cloud day first. A newer delete is applied here. An older delete is cleared. A restore publishes the restored days at the time of the restore and deletes a day the backup left out when that day was waiting to upload. An older queued delete does not rewind a newer cloud day.
